A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DBB reward-estimation work. All pages, including figures, tables, equations and appendices, are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original Qwen3 training and benchmark results, discount-factor ablations, training dynamics and empirical reward-estimation error analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds baseline comparisons, evaluation statistics, clipping controls, prior sensitivity and supplementary estimator analyses.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1, the discounted posterior updates, initialization and GRPO/Dr.GRPO integration remain unchanged. The wider DBB clipping range was already disclosed in v1; v2 investigates it without changing the proposed procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions train on DAPO-Math-17k and retain the same six mathematical and three general-reasoning evaluation benchmarks. The additional 0.6B model uses existing benchmarks; continuous and dense rewards are discussed only as future work.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds evaluated GRESO and DAPO baselines alongside GRPO and RePO. Appendices H–I additionally compare DBB with per-prompt EMA, Laplace smoothing and empirical Bayes on estimation MSE. These substantially broaden the comparator set.

E3.justification: New evaluation designs include testing both GRPO and DBB under two clipping ranges, prior-parameter sweeps, Best@8 evaluation and a discount-factor search on Qwen3-0.6B-Base. The expanded main comparison explicitly matches total rollout budgets. Existing Table 5 training settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Appendices D–I investigate whether clipping explains the gains, sensitivity to prior strength, whether lower entropy harms useful response diversity, model-scale dependence of the optimal discount factor, and whether simpler estimators suffice. These address substantial questions beyond v1’s existing discount-factor, MSE and Dr.GRPO analyses.

E5.justification: v1 reports scalar benchmark scores without stated replication or significance tests. v2 reports four independent evaluation seeds, means and standard deviations, and one-sided paired t-tests over per-prompt accuracies in Table 1. Appendix C clarifies that these are evaluation repetitions, not four independent training runs.

E6.justification: Table 1 replaces earlier scores with four-evaluation-run summaries. Reported DBB-minus-GRPO gains for 1.7B/8B change from 3.22/2.42 to 3.43/2.32 points in distribution and from 12.49/6.92 to 10.05/8.34 out of distribution. These are revised estimates, not demonstrated improvements from a changed method. New baseline, clipping, Best@8, prior-sensitivity and estimator-comparison results substantially expand the findings.

T1.justification: Appendices H–I add formal definitions and conditional MSE expressions for EMA, Laplace smoothing and empirical Bayes, including EMA’s historical weights. The original DBB equations and Appendix B derivation remain unchanged; the mathematical additions support the new comparator analyses.

C1.justification: The core contribution remains discounted historical reward estimation for sample-efficient RLVR. The abstract and conclusion qualify lower MSE by mild non-stationarity, while the introduction adds an appropriate-discount-factor qualification and claims statistically significant superiority over a broader baseline set.

C2.justification: v2 substantially expands explanations of how nonzero advantages on all-correct/all-incorrect groups affect exploration and why DBB needs wider clipping. It adds interpretations of prior sensitivity, preservation of useful diversity, model-dependent discount selection and the tuning-versus-MSE tradeoff with empirical Bayes. Suggested settings for 30B+ models are explicitly extrapolations.

D1.justification: Appendix C clarifies clipping conventions and per-method settings and adds implementation guidance for GRESO and DAPO. Appendices H–I specify EMA initialization and online method-of-moments fitting for the empirical-Bayes prior. Existing hardware, data filtering, optimizer settings and framework links are retained.

R1.justification: Section 5.3 and Appendices H–I newly position DBB against simpler shrinkage and shared-prior estimators. Section 6 and the cited-work set otherwise remain essentially unchanged; the Gelman reference switches editions of the same book rather than introducing a different work.

P1.justification: Targeted rewrites expand the abstract, experimental discussion and Sections 5.1–5.2, with terminology and cross-reference corrections. v2 adds acknowledgements, updates affiliation/publication text and appends new analyses, while retaining the main section order and most methodological exposition.

P2.justification: Table 1 is substantially expanded with additional baselines, uncertainty values and significance rows. v2 adds Figures 4–8 and Table 6, providing new diagnostic plots, a prior-sensitivity heatmap and estimator comparisons. Figure 6 redisplays existing Mean@8 curves alongside newly reported Best@8 curves.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens validation by addressing v1’s limited comparator set and absent uncertainty reporting. Appendix D directly tests the important clipping-range confound, while prior-sensitivity, Best@8 and alternative-estimator analyses better support the central argument. Replication covers evaluation randomness rather than training variability, and reporting inconsistencies remain, such as Appendix G claiming six benchmarks while Table 6 lists five. These limitations do not outweigh the substantial evidential gains.
